facts.claim: Non-playoff bowls keep their existing conference tie-ins for the 2026 postseason (one-year carryover).
facts.value: Bowl Season release dated April 17, 2026 (dateline San Antonio): its bowls "will continue their existing conference-bowl agreements with the FBS Division I conferences for the 2026 postseason." Exact quote, Nick Carparelli, executive director of Bowl Season: "We believe maintaining stability across the bowl system for 2026 is the most appropriate path forward given the CFP's decision to extend the current format through this upcoming season." Release adds that longer-term decisions on affiliations are expected "for the 2027 season and beyond once the CFP finalizes its future format."
facts.sourceName: Bowl Season release, as posted by the Frisco Bowl (ESPN Events)
facts.how: curl of the page, read raw text; datePublished 2026-04-17T16:00:00Z

facts.claim: SEC selection order: playoff first, then the Citrus Bowl picks, then the conference assigns the six-bowl pool.
facts.value: SEC release of Dec. 7, 2025: "the College Football Playoff committee first named the 12 teams to participate in the Playoff. Next, the Cheez-It Citrus Bowl in Orlando selected Texas from the SEC ..." then the "SEC Bowl Pool" of six games is assigned by the league. Process language: pool participants "are determined after conversations with bowl partners and discussions with school personnel in order to create a lineup of compelling bowl games" and the process helps "prevent repetitive postseason destinations when possible." 2025 was "the 12th year" of the pool, so 2026 is the 13th (derived).
facts.sourceName: Southeastern Conference (secsports.com)
facts.how: curl; article text extracted from the page data-page JSON. NOTE this is the 2025-26 release: no 2026-27 SEC release exists yet (assignments come Dec. 6).

facts.claim: Which six bowls are in the SEC pool for 2026: Texas, Music City, Liberty, Gator, ReliaQuest, plus Las Vegas (not Duke's Mayo) this year.
facts.value: SEC 2025 release: pool = Kinder's Texas Bowl, Liberty Mutual Music City Bowl, AutoZone Liberty Bowl, TaxSlayer Gator Bowl, ReliaQuest Bowl and Duke's Mayo Bowl; "In alternating years, the SRS Distribution Las Vegas Bowl replaces the Duke's Mayo Bowl in the SEC Bowl Pool." 2025 was the Mayo year. Las Vegas Bowl release June 3, 2026: the 2026 game is "a scheduled matchup featuring a team from the SEC vs. a representative from either the Big Ten, Big 12, ACC or Oregon State and Washington State (each featuring teams from the former Pac-12 Conference)."
facts.sourceName: SEC (2025 release) + Las Vegas Bowl (lvbowl.com)
facts.how: curl of both pages; two official sources agree. A FanSided table of "2025 affiliations" (Mayo ACC vs. SEC; Las Vegas Big Ten vs. Pac-12) describes LAST season and should not be used for 2026.

facts.claim: The Citrus Bowl takes the top available SEC and Big Ten teams outside the playoff.
facts.value: Citrus Bowl site: the game "will continue to host the top Big Ten and SEC teams from outside the CFP series of bowls." June 3, 2026 release: "The 81st Citrus Bowl, featuring top teams from the Southeastern and Big Ten Conferences ..." and this season "marks 35 years since the bowl adopted its current SEC vs. Big Ten format."
facts.sourceName: Citrus Bowl / Florida Citrus Sports
facts.how: curl, raw text; datePublished 2026-06-03

facts.claim: The ReliaQuest Bowl describes its own place in the order differently from the SEC.
facts.value: ReliaQuest Bowl FAQ: "The bowl generally gets the second selection after the CFP Bowls from the SEC and the Big Ten Conference. Factors such as the the number of SEC and Big Ten CFP playoff selections may adjust this selection order. The bowls Team Selection Committee makes a recommendation to the bowls Board of Directors which has the final decision. No decision will be made prior to the final regular season and conference championship games being played ..." (page still carries 2025 dates). The SEC describes the ReliaQuest as one of six pool games the league assigns.
facts.sourceName: ReliaQuest Bowl (reliaquestbowl.com)
facts.how: curl, raw text. Two official descriptions differ in emphasis: write "the SEC, working with the bowls, assigns" rather than a strict pick order after the Citrus.

facts.claim: What changed this year (bowl side).
facts.value: (1) Tie-ins carried over one year instead of a new cycle (A1). (2) Las Vegas replaces Duke's Mayo in the SEC pool (A3). (3) Citrus Bowl moves to Saturday, Jan. 2 at noon ET on ABC, "the first Saturday Citrus Bowl since 2022"; last season it was Dec. 31 at 3 p.m. ET and carried the Cheez-It name (SEC 2025 release); this season the bowl, ESPN and NCAA.com all list it simply as the "Citrus Bowl" (cheezitcitrusbowl.com now redirects to citrusbowlorlando.com). (4) Camping World Stadium "will host the event at a reduced capacity as the venue undergoes a $400 million renovation set for completion in 2027." (5) Gator Bowl moves from Dec. 27 at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC (2025, per SEC release) to Wednesday, Dec. 30 at 11:30 a.m. ET on ESPN. (6) Music City Bowl: "expected to be one of the last major football games played in the current Nissan Stadium," new stadium "projected to open next door in early 2027."
facts.sourceName: Citrus Bowl; SEC; Music City Bowl; ESPN
facts.how: curl of each bowl page plus SEC 2025 release. Do not state WHY the Citrus has no title sponsor in its name: no source read explains it.

facts.claim: What changed this year (playoff side).
facts.value: ESPN (Bonagura/Schlabach, Nov. 23): "New to the 2026 season, the Power 4 conference champions will receive automatic bids to the College Football Playoff along with the highest-ranked Group of 6 team regardless of whether it is a league champ. The remaining slots in the 12-team field will go to the next seven highest-ranked teams. Notre Dame is guaranteed a spot in the field if it is among the top 12 teams." NCAA.com says the same and adds the four highest-ranked teams get byes. Still 12 teams in 2026-27.
facts.sourceName: ESPN; NCAA.com
facts.how: ESPN content API (content.core.api.espn.com/v1/sports/news/50564492) + curl of https://www.ncaa.com/news/football/article/2026-08-11/how-college-football-playoff-works-schedule-selections-rankings-byes-and-more

facts.claim: This is the last bowl season before the playoff doubles.
facts.value: ESPN, Heather Dinich, Nov. 9, 2026: "The College Football Playoff has officially doubled in size, introducing a 24-team field that will start in time for the 2027 season," a change that will "eliminate Power 4 conference championship games ... and have a trickle-down effect on bowl season." The CFP site links "About the 24-Team CFP Format (Beginning 2027-28)." Florida AD Scott Stricklin, quoted by ESPN in that story: "I would say that bowls even more so are going to be like the NIT is now, which there's still teams that like playing, and they're excited for the opportunity, and some not as much, depending on where they are in their program."
facts.sourceName: ESPN (Heather Dinich)
facts.how: ESPN content API (id 50433738), full text read. Quote is usable only with attribution to ESPN.

facts.claim: Bowl math: how many SEC teams need a non-playoff bowl.

SEC sixth pool bowl: a FanSided table of 2025 affiliations shows Mayo as the SEC game; the Las Vegas Bowl's own 2026 release and the SEC's alternating-years language make it Las Vegas this season.

ReliaQuest Bowl says it "generally gets the second selection" from the SEC; the SEC says it assigns six pool bowls after the Citrus picks. Do not print a strict 1-2-3 order beyond playoff, then Citrus, then the pool.
ESPN lists Florida as both "5th in SEC" and "6th in SEC" on different endpoints. By record it sits behind five teams (5-4, tied with Kentucky, whom it beat).
CBS Sports counts 47 postseason games; ESPN's schedule story slug says 46. Avoid a game count.

The Texas Bowl's own site (would not load) and the ACC's June 3, 2026 bowl release (403): so the 2026 opponent tie-ins for the Texas, Liberty and Duke's Mayo bowls rest on last year's SEC release, CBS Sports labels and the one-year carryover.

storyNotes.primaryStorySpine: Who picks when (playoff, Citrus, then the league's pool of six: ReliaQuest, Gator, Music City, Texas, Liberty, Las Vegas); the math (12 SEC teams eligible, four headed to the playoff, eight for seven good seats, with Birmingham and Gasparilla below); the crowd at 7-4 (six teams) and what today plus Oklahoma-Missouri do to it; what the people paid to guess are guessing (Gator Bowl, five of five read); dates and sites; Florida's history in each; announcement Dec. 6.
inferencesToLabelAsAnalysis: At 8-4 Florida would be level with the Oklahoma-Missouri winner and ahead of any 7-5 team; Oklahoma is ranked higher and won in Gainesville.
At 7-5 Florida would trail at least one 8-4 SEC team and could slide in the pool; 7-5 sent Florida to the Gasparilla Bowl in 2024.
A ReliaQuest assignment would be a third bowl at Raymond James Stadium in six seasons (2021, 2024); the SEC says it tries to avoid repeat destinations.
A Citrus Bowl on Jan. 2, 2027 would be Florida's first January bowl since the Outback Bowl on Jan. 2, 2017, 10 years to the day.
storyNotes.secondPieceCandidate: Only one piece of ground none of the seven stories covers: this is the last bowl season before the 24-team playoff starts in 2027, with Florida AD Scott Stricklin telling ESPN bowls will be "like the NIT is now." It reads better as the closing section of the explainer than as a separate story, and the controller should first check whether we covered the Nov. 9 announcement.
